patterns_data.what_is_impacting: VA Medicaid / TANF Standard / ACUTE HOSPITAL / IP Med/Surg
patterns_data.pattern_details: VA cost growth is being driven by a very small number of catastrophic inpatient leukemia cases, not by a broad hospital trend. The largest episode added roughly $1.9M from a single claim, with another leukemia diagnosis adding about $357K from two claims. The operational view shows the largest spend sitting in TANF Standard at an acute hospital, so case management, payment validation, and admission review should be coordinated on the same episodes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A handful of ultra-high-cost admissions can materially distort the market and require different action than broad utilization management.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a case-level review of the VA leukemia admissions to confirm diagnosis coding, catastrophic payment handling, level of care, and contract terms before taking any broader product action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in a few low-baseline claims, so coding and payment accuracy should be confirmed before treating it as a sustained utilization pattern.
evidence_summary: One VA IP Med/Surg leukemia case tied to C9201 added about +$1.9M.
Two additional VA leukemia-related claims tied to C9250 added about +$357K.
The operational view places the largest episode in VA TANF Standard at ACUTE HOSPITAL with about +$1.9M.

key_driver_codes: Other Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue O.R. Procedures with CC

patterns_data.pattern_details: A second major theme is repeated acute hospital pressure across several Medicaid products and states, with both extra claims and higher paid amounts per episode contributing. The pattern is spread across TANF Standard, ABD Non Dual, LTSS Non Dual, and Family Care, which makes it more actionable than a one-off state anomaly. This looks like case-level admission and reimbursement pressure concentrated in acute hospitals.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Because the same acute hospital mechanism appears across multiple products and states, it can signal a repeatable utilization and payment issue rather than a single market exception.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Prioritize a multi-state acute hospital worklist for UM and reimbursement teams to validate admission necessity, outlier payment treatment, and contract terms for the named diagnoses and DRGs.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Most of the increase is concentrated in a small number of episodes with low historical baseline, so confirm claim accuracy while reviewing utilization and reimbursement levers.
evidence_summary: OH TANF Standard at ACUTE HOSPITAL added about +$416K.
KS ABD Non Dual at ACUTE HOSPITAL added about +$260K.
CA / DC / MO TANF Standard at ACUTE HOSPITAL added about +$233K.
CA LTSS Non Dual added about +$110K, with smaller acute hospital pockets in CA ABD Non Dual and MD Family Care.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Post-acute nursing facility pressure in CA / NY, with NY SNF concentration
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: CA / NY Medicaid / NF and SNF - FREE STANDING
patterns_data.pattern_details: Post-acute cost pressure is showing up in nursing facility settings, with the clearest operational concentration in NY free-standing SNF and a parallel NF case-mix signal across CA / NY. The biggest drivers are traumatic injury and connective tissue cases, suggesting discharge destination and post-acute intensity may be part of the cost story. This is a site-of-care and provider-mix issue more than a broad acute inpatient trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: When complex cases shift into NF or SNF, cost control depends on discharge planning, placement rules, and post-acute reimbursement management.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Audit NY SNF placement, length-of-stay management, and reimbursement for the named trauma and connective tissue cases, while clinically reviewing the CA / NY NF cohort for avoidable post-acute intensity.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Part of the signal is concentrated in small cohorts and includes one invalid procedure value, so the post-acute pattern should be confirmed while operational action begins.
evidence_summary: CA / NY NF traumatic injury tied to T148XXS added about +$180K across 11 claims.
CA / NY NF connective tissue disorder tied to M069 added about +$110K across 5 claims.
NY ABD Non Dual at SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$161K across 10 claims.
NY TANF Standard at the same SNF setting added another +$18K.

patterns_data.top_pattern: VERACYTE lab spend is obscured by Not Mapped classification
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: NC / IA / MO / TN / WA Medicaid / OP Lab/Pthlgy and Not Mapped facility classification
patterns_data.pattern_details: VERACYTE spend is appearing under Not Mapped facility or service classification across multiple states, with the clearest clinical concentration in NC outpatient lab and pathology. Because the same provider also appears in operational Not Mapped buckets, this is a gating data-quality and routing issue before drawing strong conclusions about utilization or reimbursement. The current classification can hide the real site of care, benefit rules, and authorization pathway.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If mapping is wrong, the business can misfire on UM, provider, and pricing actions because the claims are not being interpreted in the right service category.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Correct the facility and service mapping for VERACYTE claims, then re-run authorization, edit, and reimbursement review on the cleaned category before taking provider or utilization action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern repeatedly involves Not Mapped values and unmapped classification, so data validation is required before using it as a true provider performance signal.
evidence_summary: NC outpatient lab and pathology tied to VERACYTE added about +$58K, mostly from diagnoses E042 and E041.
Operational Not Mapped VERACYTE spend added about +$42K across NC, MO, and IA.
A separate utilization-only Not Mapped signal added about +$17K across WA and TN.
All contributing groups carry Not Mapped or unmapped flags.

patterns_data.top_pattern: TX CHILDRENS admissions are a reimbursement issue, not a volume issue
patterns_data.pattern_details: Texas CHILDRENS spend rose even though claim volume fell, which makes this a reimbursement or case-rate issue rather than a utilization spike. The single identified driver is a connective tissue disorder admission with a large increase in paid per admission. This calls for focused payment review, not broad authorization tightening.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Unit-cost-led increases need a different response than volume growth and can point to contract or payment logic issues.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review TX CHILDRENS reimbursement terms, outlier handling, and claim pricing for the named admission to confirm why paid per admit increased so sharply.
evidence_summary: TX TANF Standard at CHILDRENS added about +$91K.
Claim volume fell by 1 while paid per admit increased by about $125K.
The signal is concentrated in Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC.

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: VA Medicaid / LTSS Dual Eligible / SNF - FREE STANDING
patterns_data.pattern_details: A smaller but distinct VA pocket is emerging in LTSS Dual Eligible free-standing SNF, tied to connective tissue disorder cases. The dollar impact is modest compared with the inpatient spike, but the setting and product make it operationally different and worth targeted follow-up. This is best handled as an early post-acute management issue.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Small emerging SNF pockets can become recurring spend if placement and stay management are not addressed early.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Complete a focused audit of the VA LTSS Dual Eligible SNF cases to confirm placement appropriateness and whether a tighter post-acute management approach is needed for this diagnosis group.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The increase comes from a small low-baseline cluster, so validate the cases while determining whether this is an emerging recurring pattern.
evidence_summary: VA LTSS Dual Eligible at SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$58K across 8 claims.
Paid per admit increased by about $7K.
The increase is concentrated in Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC.
